Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, who has traveled to Tehran for talks with senior Iranian officials on bilateral relations and regional developments, met and held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Thursday afternoon. Welcoming the continued efforts by regional countries and Iran’s neighbors to help reduce tensions, Araghchi said the current situation is solely the result of U.S. and Israeli military aggression, as well as the continued illegal and interventionist actions by the United States, particularly its maritime blockade and economic terrorism against Iran. Referring to Iran’s principled position on the need to strengthen trust among regional countries in order to establish indigenous regional security mechanisms independent of interference by external actors, Araghchi noted that achieving this goal requires all regional countries to adhere to the principle of good neighborliness and prevent the United States from using their territories and facilities to prepare for and carry out acts of aggression, as well as economic warfare against Iran. Referring to the insecurity imposed on the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the U.S.-Israeli military aggression against Iran—which, regrettably, was accompanied and facilitated by some regional countries—Araghchi stressed that it is impossible to speak of returning to the situation that existed before May 31, 2026, without taking into account the realities on the ground as well as the crimes committed against Iran and the damage inflicted on the country. Araghchi emphasized that Iran had been implementing its commitments under the War Termination Memorandum in good faith, including Clause 5, but that the United States disrupted the implementation process by reneging on its commitments. He added that Washington had recently revealed its hostility and animosity toward the Iranian people more clearly than ever by announcing a new wave of economic terrorism. Araghchi stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran is resolute and steadfast in pursuing its national interests and security and will use all available capacities to defend its national sovereignty and interests. For his part, Qatar’s prime minister and foreign minister, referring to his country’s principled position on safeguarding regional security and stability, stressed the importance of continuing consultations to reduce tensions and insecurity in the region.

item.title: Qatari PM FM to visit Tehran on Thursday
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baqaei has announced that Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, will visit Tehran on Thursday. According to Baqaei, the visit is part of ongoing Iran-Qatar consultations aimed at expanding bilateral relations and strengthening regional peace and security. Referring to Qatar’s good offices in recent months to help prevent further escalation in the region following the military aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran, Baqaei said the Qatari Prime Minister will hold discussions with Iranian officials on the continuation of Qatar’s mediation efforts and initiatives, as well as other regional developments.

item.title: Iran offers condolences to families of victims of Islamabad hospital fire
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baqaei, referring to a fire in the maternity ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital in Islamabad, expressed the condolences and sympathy of the Iranian government and people to the families of the victims, as well as to the government and people of the neighboring and friendly country. Baqaei prayed to Almighty God to grant patience and endurance to the grieving fathers and mothers and wished the injured a swift recovery and good health.

item.title: Joint Statement between the Sultanate of Oman and The Islamic Republic of Iran following the consultations between the foreign ministers of the Sultan
item.description: His Excellency Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi paid a working visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran, where he held constructive consultations with his Iranian counterpart, His Excellency Dr. Seyed Abbas Araghchi. The consultations focused on the importance both countries attach to the resumption of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while preserving their sovereignty and sovereign rights. The two Ministers discussed a phased framework that could provide a practical and implementable basis for moving forward, in light of the current situation in the Strait resulting from the recent war and its tragic repercussions. The proposed framework includes the establishment of a joint temporary navigational corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines. Technical negotiations between the two sides would continue with a view to agreeing on a permanent navigational corridor and future administration of the Strait, as well as a mechanism for information-sharing, traffic management, and the provision of relevant navigational and security services. In this context, both sides underscored the importance of convening joint discussions with regional states bordering the waters of the Persian Gulf. They further stressed the need to uphold applicable international law and respect the sovereign rights of the coastal states.

item.title: Pakistan Army chief to visit Tehran
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei, speaking to reporters, announced that Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan, will travel to Tehran. Simultaneously with the anniversary of the infamous coup of 28 Mordad 1332 (19 August 1953), the ruling establishment of the United States claimed to impose extensive economic and commercial sanctions against the Iranian nation. This action is not only another sign of the continuation of 73 years of hostility and enmity by American policymakers toward the Iranian people, but also proof of the anti-human, law-breaking, and arrogant nature of the US ruling establishment. Without a doubt, the US economic sanctions against Iran, which target the fundamental human rights of every single Iranian citizen, constitute an instance of “economic terrorism” and a “crime against humanity,” and the instigators and perpetrators of these sanctions, due to the commission of such heinous crimes, deserve to be tried and punished. These sanctions, which come in the wake of the American-Zionist imposed wars of the past year and a half against Iran and the failure to advance their demonic goals of forcing the Iranian nation to surrender to their illegal and anti-human ambitions, merely lengthen the list of crimes committed by the United States against Iran. Yet they will undoubtedly have not the slightest effect on the determination of Iranians to safeguard Iran’s independence, dignity, and national sovereignty. Sanctions and economic pressure are the other side of the coin of war and military aggression, and America’s pathological addiction to these two has not only placed global peace and security under tangible threat but has also plunged human civilization into an unprecedented moral degeneration. Accordingly, any government that believes in the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, including the principle of respect for the national sovereignty of states, cannot remain indifferent to the continuation of America’s blatant law-breaking and confrontation with fundamental international norms. America’s action in pompously announcing the new sanctions, while amounting to an explicit admission of committing a crime against humanity, is the continuation of a policy that has already been tested and failed. Re-testing it will certainly yield no result other than a repetition of past failures and the disgrace of the designers and perpetrators of this policy. Of course, responsibility for its consequences and repercussions will rest with the US government and the designers and executors of this policy. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while strongly condemning America’s action in intensifying the illegal and anti-human sanctions against the Iranian nation, emphasizes that the Islamic Republic of Iran is steadfast and determined in defending its security and national interests and in confronting America’s military, economic, political, and psychological assaults and pressures. Relying on its unparalleled national capabilities and taking into account the experiences of seven decades of all-out resistance against America’s policy of pressure, intervention, military aggression, and state terrorism against Iran, the Islamic Republic of Iran will utilize all tools and capacities to repel the evil of the American-Zionist enemy and to safeguard Iran’s national interests.

item.title: Iran Mauritania FMs discuss regional developments bilateral ties
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Mauritanian Foreign Minister Mohamed Salem Ould Merzouk held a telephone conversation on Wednesday afternoon, discussing the latest regional developments and bilateral relations. Araghchi underscored the importance of strengthening cooperation among Islamic countries, particularly within the framework of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), to support Palestine and counter Israeli regime plots targeting the interests of the Islamic world. Ould Merzouk conveyed the greetings of the Mauritanian president to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, stressing Iran’s important and influential role in the OIC. He also highlighted Mauritania’s commitment to strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation with Iran, both bilaterally and within the OIC. The two sides reaffirmed their readiness to further develop bilateral relations and to cooperate and extend mutual support in international forums.
